Main points that recur across the sources:

- **Write a specific description.** Claude decides whether to use a skill from its description, so a loose one can mean the skill never triggers. A vague description means the Skill will never be activated.
- **Keep SKILL.md lean and split out detail.** One guide suggests putting essentials and navigation in SKILL.md, detailed references and examples in support files, and utilities in scripts that run without loading their code into context (SKILL.md: Essential information, quick start, navigation).
- **Restrict tools when a skill doesn't need them.** The `allowed-tools` frontmatter field can limit what a skill may use, such as a read-only review skill (Use allowed-tools to restrict capabilities).
- **Loading is on demand.** At startup Claude reads only each skill's name and description, and pulls in the full body when a request calls for it (at startup only the name and description of each skill are loaded. The full SKILL.md only gets read when relevant.). That is why a short, focused body matters.
- **Anthropic's own guidance.** An Anthropic post titled "Lessons from building Claude Code: How we use skills" covers the internal team's tips, but the retrieved text cut off before those tips appeared.

Treat the third-party guides as secondary. Check the official Claude Code skills documentation before relying on specific frontmatter fields.

The search didn't return Anthropic's own authoring best-practices page, so these results come from Anthropic's engineering post and secondary write-ups.

- **Progressive disclosure is the core design principle.** Anthropic's engineering post frames it as a layered approach, like a manual with a table of contents, chapters, and an appendix. Progressive disclosure is the core design principle that makes Agent Skills flexible and scalable.
- **Level one is the metadata.** The agent's system prompt holds each skill's name and description, which tells the model when a skill applies without loading the whole thing (it provides just enough information for Claude to know when each skill should be used).
- **Level two is the body.** Claude reads the full SKILL.md only when it judges the skill relevant to the task (it will load the skill by reading its full SKILL.md into context.).
- **Level three is bundled resources.** Reference files and scripts load only when needed. One source describes the pattern as cheap metadata always resident, full instructions loaded on demand, and bundled resources loaded only when referenced (cheap metadata always resident, full instructions loaded on demand, bundled resources loaded only when referenced.).
- **Description-writing guidance (secondary source only).** A third-party spec summary says descriptions should be written in the third person, state what the skill does plus when to use it, and avoid summarizing the workflow. It attributes the last point to Anthropic's testing, where the model followed the description instead of reading the body. I couldn't confirm this against Anthropic's own docs, so verify it there before relying on it.

## Best practices for writing Claude Code skills

My two searches didn't turn up Anthropic's official authoring docs. I only got snippets of Anthropic's own posts, so much of this comes from third-party guides. Check the official docs before relying on specific details.

**1. Write a specific description.**
- Claude uses the description to decide whether to load a skill. A vague one means the skill never triggers.
- Say what the skill does and when to use it. Name concrete tasks and file types.
- One secondary source says to write it in the third person. It also says to avoid summarizing the workflow, because the model may follow the description instead of reading the body. I couldn't confirm either point against Anthropic's docs.

**2. Use progressive disclosure.** Anthropic's engineering post calls this the core design principle.
- Level 1 is the name and description, which are always in context.
- Level 2 is the SKILL.md body, loaded only when the skill looks relevant.
- Level 3 is bundled reference files and scripts, loaded only when referenced.

**3. Keep SKILL.md lean.**
- Put essentials, a quick start and navigation in SKILL.md.
- Move detailed references and examples into separate files.
- Put utilities in scripts that run without their code being loaded into context.

**4. Restrict tools where it makes sense.** Use the `allowed-tools` frontmatter field, for example to keep a review skill read-only.

**5. Learn from Anthropic's own usage.** Anthropic published "Lessons from building Claude Code: How we use skills". The search didn't return its body, so I haven't summarized it. It is worth reading directly.

I can fetch the Anthropic blog post and the official docs page and give you a verified summary if you'd like.

Sources:
- [Lessons from building Claude Code: How we use skills](https://claude.com/blog/lessons-from-building-claude-code-how-we-use-skills)
- [Claude Code Skills: The Complete Guide (2026)](https://designrevision.com/blog/claude-code-skills)
- [Claude Code Skills: The Complete Guide to Automating Software Development](https://pasqualepillitteri.it/en/news/149/claude-code-skills-complete-guide-automation-development)

- [Agent Skills: Progressive Disclosure as a System Design Pattern](https://www.newsletter.swirlai.com/p/agent-skills-progressive-disclosure)
- [Production-grade agent skills authoring guide 2026](https://noqta.tn/en/blog/production-grade-agent-skills-authoring-guide-2026)
- [Skills progressive disclosure design spec](https://agents.open-source.onhelix.ai/superpowers/specs/2026-06-03-skills-progressive-disclosure-design.html)
